386YE Spring Equinox Conclave sessions.d: Raewyn Farkas became Hand of the Healers, Eliina Lailasdottir Archmage of Night, Raficci Vicente Barossa Imperial War Mage and Bella Vicente d'Apulian Arcane Envoy. Skywise Gralka retained Archmage of Day, and a declaration of sorcery against them failed. Concords accepted Wise Rangara's aid for the Bleak Tower and the Tower of the Fall. The Conclave accepted Roshanwe's Netweaver's Eye and Estavus's survey of three Bourse seats, and endowed the Westmere Anvil to Estavus. The Shuttered Lantern, Unfettered Mind and Golden Pyramid were sent to investigate Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, Temeschwar's rats and Mareave respectively. Chastise the Foolish was licensed and Surcease of Sorrow entered Imperial Lore. Assay the Barrens and Seek for Relics failed.

n.Grendel: The Conclave endorsed Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea across the Bay of Catazar, explicitly as a means to fight the Grendel navies, and warned locals to take precautions.
n.Imperial Orcs: Following successful prospecting in Skarsind, the Golden Pyramid was sent on a similar expedition to the Imperial-controlled regions of Mareave, described as Imperial Orc territory, to discover what resources could be found.
n.Navarr: Surcease of Sorrow was entered into Imperial Lore to preserve it as a legacy for Navarr to use until their founders' dance is complete, with Morwenna Witheredrose providing the 10 thrones.
n.The League: The Order of the Unfettered Mind was sent, at a cost of 20 crystal mana, to investigate a rat problem plaguing the League territory of Temeschwar.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Lore ritual Chastise the Foolish was licensed and is no longer interdicted, while concords committed the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall to protect Urizen from the creatures of Agramant and the Bleak Tower's custodian to protect the herb gardens of Morrow, both with Wise Rangara's aid.

t.Mareave: The Golden Pyramid was dispatched, at a cost of 20 crystal mana, to explore the Imperial-controlled regions of Mareave and discover what resources can be found there.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the earlier successful prospecting in Skarsind is cited as the reason for sending the Golden Pyramid to Mareave.
t.Temeschwar: The Unfettered Mind was sent to investigate peculiar events in Temeschwar involving a plague of rats.

386YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: Seven senators were chosen in national elections, for Holberg, Karsk, Mournwold, Reikos, Sarvos, Segura and the Barrens. The Senate filled ambassadorships, generalships and many sinecures, including the Rebeshof Roadwarden. The Synod returned figures such as Hazelelponi as Lepidean Librarian with 224 votes and Ingrid as Speaker of the Crows with 220. The Military Council named Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo as Imperial Fleet Master and appointed strategoi for the Brass Coast, the Marches and Urizen. Bourse titles went at auction or by vote, with The Red Depths going to Sagremar I Zayden I Guerra on 723 votes. Hildebrand Von Holberg was made Dean of the Academy.

n.Dawn: Dawn's voters elected Aramis du Froste as Senator for the Barrens.
n.Highguard: Highguard elected Cyrus, of Ebon's Hall, as Senator for Reikos.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast elected Velasco i Guerra as Senator for Segura, and Gael i Guerra was appointed Strategos of the Brass Coast.
n.The League: The League elected Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg as Senator for Holberg and Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos as Senator for Sarvos. Several League-named sinecures were also filled, among them the Rebeshof Roadwarden and the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange.
n.The Marches: The Marches elected Simon "Chordwangler" Willow as Senator for Mournwold, and Aliss Thorn was appointed Strategos of the Marches.
n.Urizen: The Military Council appointed Lanius as Strategos of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Varushka elected Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad as Senator for Karsk.

t.Holberg: Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg. Holberg's Melodious Cascade and Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes received new holders, Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund respectively.
t.Karsk: Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad became Senator for Karsk.
t.Mournwold: Simon "Chordwangler" Willow became Senator for Mournwold.
t.Reikos: Cyrus, of Ebon's Hall, became Senator for Reikos.
t.Sarvos: Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos became Senator for Sarvos, and Wolfgang Wilheim Von Vanderghast was appointed Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange.
t.Segura: Velasco i Guerra became Senator for Segura.
t.The Barrens: Aramis du Froste became Senator for the Barrens.

r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Senate appointed Lia Adelaar as Rebeshof Roadwarden.

386YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1406 thrones. The Senate abrogated the Temple of the Four Winds, made Warmage a national Urizen title and created several new titles, including Mistress of Monuments, Shadowed Torchbearer and the Voices of Virtue. The Guerdon was set at 150 thrones. A treaty with the Rahvin, which would have ceded Barrens regions, passed but was vetoed by Empress Vesna. A one-season peace with the Druj failed. The Beoraidh treaty was passed and then amended to the agreed text. Funds went to Thornsong, the Five Cities College of War, the Caricomare flood defences and the Roads of the Sky. Kindra Surefoot, Accalon, Nikita Teanga Volkov, Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato and Ebenezer were elected ambassadors.

n.Dawn: A vetoed Rahvin treaty would have ceded the Bitter Strand and Carmine Fields of the Barrens in return for Rahvin mithril trade with Dawn. Dawn's senators also backed the Spires of Dusk remodelling and the Roads of the Sky.
n.Druj: The Senate rejected a one-season peace with the Druj that would have freed their prisoners. It commissioned a smuggler's cove in the Salt Flats of Sanath to strike at the Druj heartland and ordered Druj elements stripped from the Spires of Dusk.
n.Grendel: Under the Beoraidh treaty, Beoraidh denies the Grendel access to its shipyard and gives no direct support to their war. The Urizen of the Silver Flame also agreed to reject Grendel offers.
n.Highguard: Accalon of Highguard became Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic. The Book of the Dead was made regalia of the Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial, and Highborn senators raised the Beoraidh treaty and the Spider's Dream Bridge fortification.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Senate assigned the territory of Mareave to the Imperial Orcs. In Skarsind, the Feldspar Distillery was announced and Snowstorm Henk was sent to investigate the Sorrowful Tunnels.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; they connect to the page only through Bregasland, the territory they held, where the Eels Landing docks were commissioned.
n.Navarr: Navarr secured 50 thrones towards Thornsong, the potion research college. Their proposed Court of the Spider King in Brocéliande, which would have opened communication with Arhallogen, failed.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman's motion abrogated the Temple of the Four Winds, and Segura's Druj peace treaty failed. Graciana i Lopez i Guerra was tasked with appraising Sermersuaq's wealth, and Finna i Guerra represented the Empire in the Beoraidh treaty.
n.The League: League cities gained 100 thrones for the Five Cities College of War, 40 thrones for the Caricomare flood defences and 25 thrones for the Roads of the Sky. The Printers Guild Mausoleum and the City of Flowers works were announced, and Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato became Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
n.The Marches: Funding for the Drakes' drummers gave that army the Pride of the Marches quality, and the Happiston Mana Exchange was commissioned in the Chalkdowns. Ebenezer of the Marches was elected Ambassador to Faraden after the election was escalated to the Empress.
n.Urizen: Warmage became a national Urizen title chosen by Urizen magicians in the Hall of Worlds. The Urizen of the Silver Flame were recognised as foreigners by treaty, and the Roads of the Sky and Nostos Docks were commissioned.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators won commissions to fortify Delev, build the Inn of the Granite Stag and create the Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery in Drownbark Forest. Nikita Teanga Volkov became Ambassador to Jarm, and Empress Vesna vetoed the Rahvin treaty.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sought an appraisal of Sermersuaq's untapped wealth and gained a mana sinecure and the Iron Grove in Kallavesa. Kindra Surefoot was elected Ambassador to Otkodov.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat's senator seconded the Roads of the Sky commission.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion's senator proposed the Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic election and seconded the Sermersuaq appraisal.
t.Bregasland: Docks were commissioned at Eels Landing in the North Fens and ceded to House Greywater for their service during the occupation. The town also received a market charter, ratified by the Emperor.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's senator proposed the Voices of Virtue titles and seconded the Keeper of the Cox amendment.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's senator proposed the mana sinecure in Kallavesa and received 5 thrones for it.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia's senator proposed the failed Court of the Spider King and seconded the Faraden election and the withdrawn first Karsk counting house motion.
t.Holberg: Work continued on transforming Holberg into the City of Flowers. Holberg's senator also proposed the appraisal of the Dho'uala threat.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's senator proposed abrogating the Temple of the Four Winds and seconded the Thornsong funds.
t.Kallavesa: A mana sinecure was commissioned in Kallavesa for small halls unable to afford a wayleave, and the Iron Grove herb garden was announced in Skymark.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov's senator proposed fortifying Delev and seconded the failed Court of the Spider King.
t.Karsk: A Prosperous Counting House was announced in Karsk, self-funded by Wolfs Hearth and the Embers of Iversgaard; an earlier Senate motion for it was withdrawn.
t.Mareave: Mareave was assigned to the Imperial Orcs, and the Beoraidh treaty set terms for its regions, river access and trade. The Imperial Spymaster announced the dismantling of the Mareave spy network.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren's senator proposed the amended Beoraidh treaty and seconded the Face of the Empire power.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova's senator proposed the smuggler's cove in the Salt Flats of Sanath and seconded the Otkodov ambassador election.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold's senator proposed funding the Drakes' drummers and seconded the Silver Flame treaty.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow's senator proposed the treaty with the Urizen of the Silver Flame.
t.Mournwold: The Happiston Mana Exchange, a 16-wain mana ministry, was commissioned in the Chalkdowns. Mournwold's senator also seconded the failed Druj peace treaty.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis's senator proposed fortifying Spider's Dream Bridge and seconded the Nostos Docks.
t.Ossium: The Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery mana ministry was announced in Drownbark Forest. Ossium's senator also proposed the Shadowed Torchbearer title.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's senator proposed the Jarm ambassador election and seconded the Spires of Dusk amendment.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos's senator proposed the original Beoraidh treaty and seconded the Lepidean true liao amendment.
t.Sarvos: The Senate disbursed 40 thrones for flood defences in Caricomare, to be built with the aid of the Vandersaar.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's senator proposed the failed Druj peace treaty and seconded the Spider's Dream Bridge fortification.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm's senator proposed setting the Guerdon and seconded the appraisal of the Dho'uala threat around the Semmerlak.
t.Sermersuaq: Graciana i Lopez i Guerra was commissioned to appraise how Sermersuaq's untapped natural wealth could boost its prosperity, with findings due before the Summer Solstice.
t.Skarsind: The Feldspar Distillery herb garden was announced in Skarsind, and Snowstorm Henk was sent on a year-long investigation of the troll ruins of the Sorrowful Tunnels.
t.Spiral: Spiral received 25 thrones towards the Roads of the Sky, and the Silver Flame Urizen pledged to help defend it against the Druj or Grendel. The Spires of Dusk will be remodelled as a monument to the Hounds of Glory.
t.Tassato: Tassato gained 100 thrones for the Five Cities College of War. The Printers Guild Mausoleum was also announced there, awaiting a choice of region.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's senator proposed the Face of the Empire power and seconded the Beoraidh treaty amendment.
t.The Barrens: A Rahvin treaty ceding the Bitter Strand and Carmine Fields was vetoed, and a Druj peace that would have let the Black Wind leave the Barrens failed. The Barrens senator proposed remodelling the Spires of Dusk.
t.Therunin: Therunin's senator received 50 thrones towards completing Thornsong, the Empire's potion research college.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator proposed the vetoed Rahvin treaty and seconded the Drakes funding.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's senator secured the self-funded Inn of the Granite Stag in Veltsgorsk, letting the holder of the Granites of Veltsgorsk buy extra white granite, and seconded fortifying Delev.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater's senator seconded the smuggler's cove in the Salt Flats of Sanath.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith's senator proposed the self-funded Nostos Docks and seconded abrogating the Temple of the Four Winds.

r.Kallavesa/Skymark: The Iron Grove, a herb garden sinecure whose keeper is appointed with tenure by Wintermark's senators, was announced in Skymark.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Under the Beoraidh treaty, Ehsan and successors retain Beoraidh for at least five years, paying the Empire 50 crowns per season per region.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Beoraidh treaty commits Beoraidh to lay no claim to Fleisardh.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Under the Beoraidh treaty, Ehsan and successors retain Sinfoyard for at least five years in return for seasonal payments to the Empire.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Happiston Mana Exchange ministry was commissioned in the Chalkdowns, paid for by Morgan Townsend through Happiston Bakes.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery, a 12-mithril mana ministry, was announced in Drownbark Forest.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin treaty would have ceded the Bitter Strand, but the Empress vetoed it.

386YE Spring Equinox Synod judgements.d: Enacted mandates consecrated the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind, First Voice Glade in Miaren and Good Walder's Orchard in Mitwold, and bound Navarr by oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs. Other mandates shaped Apulian's culture, sent the Vigilant to Spiral, funded the Library of Worth and the Great Hall of Fabric Arts, and bound three Marcher armies to their home territories. Strong statements backed the Way's spread in Asavea and the fight against the Cold Sun. Hengest Dunn was revoked as senator for Hahnmark. Several figures connected to the Barrens received penances. Dogri Thulebane and Amika Acciai were escalated for exemplar recognition, and the Virtue Fund was almost exhausted by rewardings.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish assembly called its knights against the Deadwood Knight and flatly refused to offer sacrifices to Dho'uala. It also sought memorials for the ruined Towers of Dawn and asked for its fourth army to become an army of Black Knights. Several Dawnish figures received penances over their actions in the Barrens.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named as the destroyers of the Towers of Dawn and, alongside the Grendel, as raiders whom Imperial corsairs and reavers were urged to strike back against.
n.Grendel: Priests were told the Grendel plotted to weaponise the Black Plateau and to destroy a bridge between Redoubt and Necropolis. Coastal Urizen and League citizens were warned that Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea had been cast on the Bay of Catazar against them.
n.Highguard: The Highborn invited Freeborn and Marcher priests to teach at the Holy City rising in Bastion and recommitted the grey pilgrims to ending the vallorn. They also invited the Imperial Orcs to open the tomb of Emperor Ahraz and celebrated completing their reckoning with the League.
n.Imperial Orcs: Their nation gained a true consecration of Ambition at the Legion's Rookery and committed granite and coin to the Library of Worth each season for a year. Their priests marked Mareave as their second territory and warned Skarsind of a coming avalanche after the Cold Sun destroyed the home of the Storm Shaman.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a General Assembly statement recalled the Bregaslanders who sided with Mathilda Fisher and her Jotun masters.
n.Navarr: An enacted mandate bound the Navarr by oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs as family, reassuring the orcs settled in Hercynia and Miaren. The assembly also rallied artists and the people of Miaren against the Cold Sun, appointed chaplains to the thorns and scouts, and called for the liberation of Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly backed the Mareave allocation on condition their lands are returned, honoured the Marracossans who defended Madruga and urged a corsair search of ruined Free Landing. Its enacted mandate began raising the Burning Falcon to True Conviction, and the Prosperity assembly called for the Freeborn to be defended.
n.The League: An enacted Urizen mandate will slowly shape Apulian into a city of philosophy and learning. League priests were sent to protect Spiral and Apulian from a Grendel plot, and coastal citizens were warned about the curse on the Bay of Catazar. The League also declared its reckoning with Highguard complete.
n.The Marches: Oaths bound the Tusks, Drakes and Bounders to Mournwold, Mitwold and Upwold, and Good Walder's Orchard was consecrated. The assembly called off a farmers' strike, condemned Hugh Farrier's plans to curse Urizen and accepted Highborn help patrolling its borders.
n.Thule: Wintermark's assembly noted that the Thule have granted sanction to hunt the Blood on Snow cult leader Maarik Goldentongue in the Silver Peaks. A proposal to send mediators to guide freed Thule skeins was withdrawn.
n.Urizen: Urizen priests urged Spiralites to return and rebuild their spires and asked the Crucible of Fate's artisans to make heavy armour. They pledged not to retaliate in kind for Marcher curses. A narrowly upheld General Assembly statement opposed making the Warmage a national title, though the Senate made it an Urizen one.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan assembly hailed the defence of Delev and called for Cold Sun remnants to be rooted out and for units to band together against the Schlacta of Rot. It defended the Iron Helms and enacted a mandate funding the Great Hall of Fabric Arts each season. Dawn's assembly rejected Varushkan traditions regarding Dho'uala.
n.Wintermark: The assembly revoked Hengest Dunn as senator for Hahnmark and added Thanmir Hrafnar to the Chronicle of Heroes. It also called on Winterfolk hunters to kill Maarik Goldentongue. Dogri Thulebane's recognition as an exemplar of Loyalty was escalated to the General Assembly.

t.Bastion: The Grand Inspiration of the Way is being raised here. The Highborn invited delegations of Freeborn Sutannir and Marcher monks and friars to teach in Bastion once it is completed.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: a statement recalled Bregaslanders siding with Mathilda Fisher, and a bid to rename Fisher's Rock as Amberlain's Stand was withdrawn.
t.Brocéliande: The Dawnish assembly urged its knights to quest into the vallorn-infested Greenwood to claim the bounty uncovered by the Emerald Dogs.
t.Karov: Southern Karov is threatened by the Deadwood Knight and its people by remnants of the Blade of Skies. Varushka committed 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns each season to the Great Hall of Fabric Arts here. Karov's senator was inquisited and given penance.
t.Madruga: The Freeborn thanked the Marracossans of Trajadoz for defending Madruga against the Grendel and warned citizens to avoid the spreading blight. Everburning flames from Madruga are to help raise the Burning Falcon's quality.
t.Mareave: Priests described Mareave as newly under Imperial control and allocated to the Imperial Orcs. They urged pilgrims to spread the Way there, and the Freeborn expected their lands to be returned in time.
t.Miaren: First Voice Glade received a true consecration of Pride. Navarri artists were urged to decorate the trees petrified by the Empty Hands, and an enacted mandate rewards units supporting armies that fight that Cold Sun host here with herbs.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: notes on a Highborn call to breed blood whelks identify them with the frigid waters of the Sea of Snows near Caitun.
t.Skarsind: The Legion's Rookery was consecrated to Ambition, and the septs will fund the Library of Worth. The Imperial Orc assembly warned that the Cold Sun had destroyed the Storm Shaman's home and that an avalanche was coming.
t.Spiral: Urizen priests called exiled Spiralites home to rebuild their spires. An enacted mandate sent the Vigilant here to root out threats, and League and Urizen priests were urged to protect citizens against a Grendel plot involving the Black Plateau.
t.The Barrens: The Great Forest Orcs, reassured by Navarr's oath, are mostly returning home. Several senators and a general received penances over Imperial actions here, and Dawn's assembly sought proposals to memorialise the ruined Towers of Dawn.
t.The Semmerlak: The Assembly of Nine directed the Silent Bell to investigate how to counter the sovereign Dho'uala. Dawn refused any sacrifices to it, and Lady Amicia of the Semmerlak was called to inquisition over the matter.
t.Therunin: The Navarr assembly urged research into how liao was first refined from vinum here. Some Great Forest Orcs will stay in Therunin even as most return to the Heart of Peytaht.
t.Weirwater: Northern Weirwater is terrorised by the Deadwood Knight. The Dawnish assembly called on knights to slay it, and the House of Fools offered it a test of mettle.
t.Zenith: The Urizen assembly asked the artisans of the Crucible of Fate to turn from making light armour to heavy armour. The Golden Pyramid was praised for helping empower the Crucible.

r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Navarr pledged to guide Highborn exploring the Terunael ruins, and Highguard resolved to send units to explore them after grey pilgrims rescued Navarr thorns.
r.Karov/Duzekani: Varushka's assembly declared that Delev stands and Duzekani is burnt but Imperial. It called for recognition of the Dawnish, Navarr and Varushkan heroes who defended it.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Freeborn assembly urged the Red Wind Corsairs to search the ruins of the Shining Pillar for Guerra's crystal. The site is now a maelstrom with no rubble to search.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge was cited as Dogri Thulebane's legacy, the site of his stand at Crow's Keep before the Thule took it, in the recognition escalating him as an exemplar of Loyalty.
r.Spiral/Screed: The League assembly warned citizens to avoid the Black Plateau in Screed. Urizen and League priests were sent to protect citizens against a Grendel plot to weaponise it.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Under Navarr's enacted oath, most of the Great Forest Orcs sheltering in Therunin will return to the Heart of Peytaht. A rival mandate to protect all who call Peytaht home, orc and human alike, was not enacted.

386YE Spring Equinox event schedule.d: Six nations had senatorial elections: the Brass Coast, Dawn, Highguard, the League, the Marches and Varushka. Eight nations held Tally of the Votes elections for national titles. Friday's business included an Imperial Seer scrying, the Muster, Conclave and a 10pm Senate session. Saturday brought a battle off Anvil at 11am, the Bourse auction, the election of the Doyen of the Spires, Grandmaster elections, a Druj Delegation in the Senate Building and further Senate sessions. Sunday featured another battle off Anvil, a Military Council session, an Academy graduation and a final Senate session at 2pm. The Synod was open for judgement at intervals throughout.

n.Dawn: Dawn's new player meeting was set for 2:45pm, and the nation was due to elect a senator for The Barrens.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Druj Delegation was scheduled in the Senate Building at 5:30pm on Saturday.
n.Highguard: Highguard held its new player meeting at 2pm, elected a senator for Reikos and chose the Bursar of the House of Spirits by Tally of the Votes at the Chapel at 3:30pm.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs elected the Steel Fist, the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post and the Steward of the Mines of Gulhule at the Fire Pit at 5:30pm.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held its new player meeting at 2pm, elected a senator for Segura and, at the Waypoint at 4:30pm, chose the Cerevado Nets, The Red Depths, the Marracossa Sendito and the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel.
n.The League: The League held its new player meeting at 2:30pm, elected senators for Holberg and Sarvos and chose the Tassatan Hills and Custodian of the Assayer's Guild titles at the Plaza at 5pm.
n.The Marches: The Marches held its new player meeting at 1:30pm, elected a senator for Mournwold and chose the Alder of Meade at the Community Hall at 4:30pm.
n.Urizen: Urizen elected the Gloaming Merchant and the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks near the Net of Heaven at 5:30pm.
n.Varushka: Varushka held its new player meeting at 1:45pm, elected a senator for Karsk and, at the Central Hearth at 4pm, chose the Gift of the Dwindling Star, the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore and the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark elected the Keeper of the Runegrott, the Talon of Kauppahall, the Mediator of Wreck and the Mediator of Fisk at the Tree of Names at 3:30pm.

t.Holberg: The League was due to elect a senator for Holberg at this summit.
t.Karsk: Varushka was due to elect a senator for Karsk at this summit.
t.Mournwold: The Marches was due to elect a senator for Mournwold at this summit.
t.Reikos: Highguard was due to elect a senator for Reikos at this summit.
t.Sarvos: The League was due to elect a senator for Sarvos, with the next regular election for the seat falling at the Summer Solstice 386YE.
t.Segura: The Brass Coast was due to elect a senator for Segura at this summit.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting was among the Imperial Orc titles elected by Tally of the Votes.
t.The Barrens: Dawn was due to elect a senator for The Barrens at this summit.

386YE Spring Equinox interlude.d: Wintermark units were urged to protect their people through a harsh winter and against Agramant. Imperial Orc and Highborn units could join the Bone Pilgrimage, Navarr units could become roadwardens, and any unit could scout the vallorn heart at Bendol. Freeborn fleets could escort shipping in the Bay of Catazar against the Grendel. Icy Maw halved Urizen mana production, the Serpent's Curse weakened Urizen congregations, Tharim's black frost drained the Brass Coast, and Dho'uala hampered Semmerlak fleets. League culture drew pilgrims and enriched congregations and artistic sinecures. Contributions opened for Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial in Necropolis, and two new rituals entered Imperial Lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets continued to suffer a one-rank production penalty from Dho'uala in the Semmerlak, while the Queen's Rose sinecure at the Rose Towers gained an extra 108 rings from visitors.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a spy network at Bendol sought to learn how the Druj had contained the vallorn heart in Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: Brass Coast fleets were mandated to protect Imperial shipping in the Bay of Catazar from Grendel ships, and the earlier penalty the Grendel imposed on fleets there was removed.
n.Highguard: Highborn military units could join the Bone Pilgrimage, and contributions opened for Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial in Necropolis, due for completion by the Summer Solstice.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc military units could join the Bone Pilgrimage to find the remains of orc ancestors and return them to the Bone Ossuary in Skarsind.
n.Navarr: A Navarr assembly mandate let Navarr military units become roadwardens, keeping Imperial roads safe from small-scale threats in return for rings and resources.
n.The Brass Coast: Ahraz i Guerra's mandate opened an escort adventure for Brass Coast fleets, but Tharim's black frost cost every Brass Coast mana site and herb garden production until the Summer Solstice in return for knights supporting the Fire of the South. The Azure Chorus and Crimson Drummers each gained 108 rings.
n.The League: Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra's mandate drew art pilgrims to Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar, enriching their congregations, while Holberg's fleets continued to suffer Dho'uala's penalty.
n.Urizen: Icy Maw halved mana production in Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith, and the Serpent's Curse cost every Urizen congregation two votes and one liao until the Winter Solstice 386YE. Urizen alone did not recognise the Bone Pilgrimage.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets continued to suffer a one-rank production penalty from Dho'uala, and a Varushkan assembly mandate encouraged priests to help with the Bone Pilgrimage.
n.Wintermark: Assembly mandates rewarded Wintermark military units that hunted the Suaq Wastes or defended Wintermark and penalised those that did not, while Sermersuaq farms gained a production bonus through the harsh winter.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel penalty on fleets in the bay was lifted, and Brass Coast fleets could take an adventure escorting Imperial shipping while avoiding battle with the Grendel.
t.Holberg: Fleets based in Holberg continued to lose one rank of production to the terror of Dho'uala in the Semmerlak.
t.Kahraman: As Brass Coast land, Kahraman's mana sites and herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost, while the Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse gained extra income from visitors.
t.Kallavesa: The Custodian of the Ivarsgard Docks still faced cerulean mazzarine prices raised by a fifth as Dho'uala's presence disrupted trade.
t.Madruga: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga drew larger audiences and gained 108 rings, though Brass Coast mana sites and herb gardens suffered Tharim's frost.
t.Morrow: Icy Maw halved Morrow's mana site production and its mana-producing sinecures' income this season.
t.Necropolis: Resources could be donated towards Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial in Necropolis, which would become effectively a folly if at least ten wains were given.
t.Redoubt: Icy Maw halved Redoubt's mana site production and its mana-producing sinecures' income this season.
t.Sarangrave: A temporary spy network at Bendol offered to investigate the vallorn heart, how the Druj had contained it, and the risks of tying it into the network.
t.Sarvos: Art pilgrims flocked to Sarvos, and every congregation there received an additional 36 rings.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq farms gained a one-rank production bonus, and Sermersuaq-based units hunting the Suaq Wastes gained a +2 strength bonus, as the people kept each other safe through the harsh winter.
t.Skarsind: Orc ancestors' remains gathered on the Bone Pilgrimage were to be returned to Skarsind and interred at the Bone Ossuary.
t.Tassato: Art pilgrims flocked to Tassato, and every congregation there received an additional 36 rings.
t.Temeschwar: Art pilgrims flocked to Temeschwar, and every congregation there received an additional 36 rings.
t.The Semmerlak: The sovereign Dho'uala's presence still hampered fleets on the lake, and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak remained unable to buy ilium and paid more for weirwood.
t.Zenith: Icy Maw halved the production of every mana site in Zenith this season.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse drew more visitors to its performances and gained an additional 108 rings.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Any military unit could support a temporary spy network in Bendol scouting the vallorn heart, though without reward.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Wintermark units based in Sermersuaq that hunted the Suaq Wastes gained a +2 bonus to effective strength.

386YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Empress Vesna's address coincided with Empire-wide festivities. The Jotun were banished from Bregasland, and Urizeni rebels in Spiral pressed their demands. A curse war between Urizen and the Marches brought storms to the southern coast and snow to Urizen. Imperial victory in Clisearn left the Senate to assign Mareave, where Eoradal was ceded through a conjunction. The Schlacta of Rot rampaged between Karov and Weirwater. The Black Wind returned to the Barrens, and rats plagued Temeschwar. Writs of consecration offered memorials to Gerallt Brackensong, Thrace and Good Walder. Conjunction heroes defeated Grendel raiders and the Scions in many regions. However, the Shining Pillar was destroyed, Oath-heart was corrupted, and Jotun slaughtered Feni in Liathaven.

n.Dawn: Dawnish lands faced the Deadwood Knight's growing undead rampage in Weirwater and a tense standoff in the Barrens, where the Black Wind returned. In Astolat, the Scions were defeated and the Castle of Thorns' rose garden was saved.
n.Druj: In the Barrens, isolated septs began reaching out to one another as Spring arrived, and the Druj were among those approached.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Clisearn and ceded Eoradal in Mareave, were beaten by heroes at Coursmouth, Naris, Uccelini and Lightsea, and were stopped from looting the Lyceum. The Senate's appraisal sought ways to strike at their navies, and the port of Oran stayed closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: Highborn wayfarers spread the Doctrine of Enlightenment abroad, and Highborn priests were active in the Marches. At home, Grendel were defeated in Coursmouth, but Oath-heart in Bastion was corrupted and remained in the Scions' hands.
n.Imperial Orcs: Senate-funded prospecting in Skarsind uncovered lucrative opportunities and mysteries, and the civil service concluded that Thrace's memorial belonged in Skarsind. The orcs also weighed building a cultural monument in defiance of Cold Sun.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were banished from Bregasland and the Jarl of Greenwall was killed at Iron Stand. In Liathaven, however, a Jotun warband went unstopped and is assumed to have slaughtered a Feni settlement.
n.Navarr: The Navarr gained an opportunity for a memorial to Gerallt Brackensong, saw the Dance of Navarr and Thorn performed in Therunin, and had Goldglades' forests protected. Their Black Wind army returned to the Barrens, and they insisted the war with Cold Sun in Miaren was not yet done.
n.The Brass Coast: An appraisal found the Dry Patricians trying to spread their blight beyond Madruga, where the Lyceum was saved but the Shining Pillar was destroyed. Kahraman enjoyed soothing Spring rains, and Erdene Bataguin was rescued there.
n.The League: The League faced open Urizeni rebellion in Spiral and a rat plague in Temeschwar, and Holberg considered building a giant temple-orphanage. Grendel were defeated at Glass Point Cove in Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marches celebrated the Jotun's banishment from Bregasland but were embroiled in a curse war with Urizen that risked more Marchers being declared sorcerers. Good Walder memorial sites were identified in Mitwold and Upwold, and assorted developments touched all four territories.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: captive Thule warlocks were rescued from the Siroc Plains in Madruga and returned to Anvil.
n.Urizen: Urizeni rebels in Spiral fought the territory's allocation to the League, and Urizen's territories were battered by cursed snow and hail. The sword scholars scattered, ending their tradition, while Grendel were defeated near the Great Harbour of Elos.
n.Varushka: Karov suffered the Schlacta of Rot's growing undead legion. Varushka spoke of building a cultural monument, and in Miekarova the risen villagers returned contentedly to their barrow.
n.Wintermark: Two names added to the Chronicle of Heroes, one of them not from Wintermark, drew outside interest. Heroes saved New Dunhall in Hahnmark and Hufi's Glen in Kallavesa, and Wintermark fleets gained a trade bonus at Faraden.

t.Astolat: In Groveyard, heroes defeated the Scions and the rose garden of the Castle of Thorns remained.
t.Bastion: Heroes failed to reclaim Oath-heart at Tamar's Stand, and it was corrupted and remained in the Scions' hands.
t.Bay of Catazar: Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra's Senate appraisal examined how fleet captains could disrupt Grendel naval and logistical operations in the bay.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun were banished and the pretender Mathilda Fisher was dead, though some in the western fens still held grudges. The Loyalty assembly and the matter of Bushel Sykes stirred gossip.
t.Brocéliande: A knight-errant was rescued from Crangton Copse in Greenweald and returned safely to Anvil.
t.Hahnmark: The Scions were defeated at Dun's Hurst and New Dunhall stood.
t.Holberg: Hildebrand von Holberg's judgement called for a giant temple-orphanage to celebrate the greatest city in the world, and Holberg meat entrepreneurs were involved in sausage business at Anvil.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman enjoyed soft rains and verdant growth from a magnitude 40 Spring ritual, most likely Regrow the Land's Heart. Erdene Bataguin was rescued on the Path of Idina.
t.Kallavesa: The Scions were defeated on the Road to Masi, saving the apothecaries and herbalists of Hufi's Glen.
t.Karov: The Schlacta of Rot was rampaging along the Weirwater border with a growing undead retinue of perhaps two hundred or more warriors.
t.Liathaven: A Jotun warband was not stopped at the Bawn of Daffyd, and the Feni settlement there is assumed to have been slaughtered.
t.Madruga: The Dry Patricians were trying to spread their blight to neighbouring territories. The Lyceum was protected from Grendel looting, but the Shining Pillar was destroyed. Thule captives were rescued and an heirloom reclaimed.
t.Mareave: Imperial victory in Clisearn turned the tide and Eoradal was ceded, leaving the Senate to assign the territory to a nation. Conjunction efforts also paid off the Dracaild of Rathmonna and recovered the map to Rucraic's Aerie.
t.Miaren: The Navarr considered the war with Cold Sun in Miaren unfinished, though the Scions were defeated and Goldglades' forests protected.
t.Miekarova: The risen villagers of Perumaki were content that their hospitality had been accepted and returned to their barrow.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold contained locations identified for a Good Walder memorial, and its senator was tagged in Marcher developments.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the Axos remained annoyed at Imperial involvement in the failure of their joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold Orcs' ongoing transformation into Marcher orcs was among the Marcher developments discussed.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis was affected by the storms of the curse war, and the Grendel were defeated at Hedra's Meadow in Coursmouth, yielding information.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was tagged in Wintermark news and led the rescue of Thule captives.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was pummelled by cursed snow and hail, while Grendel were defeated in Naris and the Great Harbour of Elos was left unharmed.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was caught up in the curse-war storms, and Grendel were defeated at the Isle of Quiet, leaving Glass Point Cove unharmed.
t.Sermersuaq: Its people were tagged as especially concerned by the Chronicle of Heroes news and Wintermark's harsh winter.
t.Skallahn: The Jarl of Greenwall was killed at Hralfstor's Orchard, and the fyrd of Iron Stand cannot be raised until the start of Spring Equinox 387YE.
t.Skarsind: Prospecting in Skarsind's mountains proved potentially lucrative, and it was judged the only reasonable site for Thrace's memorial.
t.Spiral: Urizeni rebels were in open revolt against the territory's allocation to the League, and the Empire sought to meet their demands.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange was tagged as affected by the curse-war storms.
t.Temeschwar: Fearless rats were biting people, dogs and cats across the city, and something was rumoured to be amiss at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.
t.The Barrens: The Black Wind returned cautiously amid fear and division, but with Spring the isolated septs began reaching out to each other, including the Druj.
t.Therunin: At the Circle of Rot, the vallornspawn were distracted and the Archmage of Spring performed the Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
t.Upwold: Upwold held possible Good Walder memorial sites, and the Scions were defeated on the Heath, protecting the Sutton Stone Quarries.
t.Weirwater: The Deadwood Knight was rampaging along the Karov border, its undead legion growing and its attacks becoming bolder.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: At Tamar's Stand, Oath-heart was corrupted and remained in the Scions' hands.
r.Brocéliande/Greenweald: A knight-errant was rescued from Crangton Copse and returned to Anvil.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: The Scions were defeated at Dun's Hurst and New Dunhall stands.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: Erdene Bataguin was rescued on the Path of Idina and returned to Anvil.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The Scions were defeated on the Road to Masi, saving Hufi's Glen's apothecaries and herbalists.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The Jotun warband at the Bawn of Daffyd was not stopped, and its Feni are assumed slaughtered.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Grendel were defeated at Ezmara's Thicket and the heirloom was reclaimed.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Imperial forces conquered Clisearn, turning the tide in Mareave.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal was ceded to the Empire after the Grendel warbeasts were slaughtered.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: The Scions were defeated at the Golden Meadow and Goldglades' forests were protected.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: The risen villagers of Wilkza returned contentedly to their barrow.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Grendel were defeated at Hedra's Meadow and information was uncovered.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Grendel were defeated at the Elosian Grove and the Great Harbour of Elos was unharmed.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Grendel were defeated at the Isle of Quiet and Glass Point Cove was unharmed.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Greenwall's Jarl was killed by Imperial heroes at Iron Stand.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: The Jarl of Greenwall was killed at Hralfstor's Orchard, and Iron Stand's fyrd cannot be raised until Spring Equinox 387YE.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: At the Circle of Rot, the vallornspawn were distracted and the Dance of Navarr and Thorn was performed.
r.Upwold/The Heath: The Scions were defeated at Sammy's Paling, protecting the Sutton Stone Quarries.

386YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The scions of Cold Sun pressed their campaign of oblivion (Eclipse). Imperial armies met the Lasambrian Jotun advance in Kahraman (Below the red rock). The armies in Skallahn withdrew into Sermersuaq, leaving the Jotun to reclaim lost land. Five armies fought in Beoraidh as the Empire pushed to conquer Mareave's Broken Shore (Sea-wood fed with copper), and Imperial forces fought to reclaim Madruga from those who burned Siroc (The cry of gulls). The Military Council would choose two of four battles: Liathaven and Kallavesa against the Jotun, Mareave and Madruga against the Grendel. Conjunctions included vallornspawn in Brocéliande and Hercynia, marked Patricians in Segura and Kahraman, and scions in several territories.

n.Dawn: Dawn could commit substantial forces to the season's battles, though its armies may not take the Cautious Advance or Give Ground orders. The Reeve of Greenforest Fair was asked to lead Dawnish heroes against vallornspawn in Brocéliande, and two conjunctions arose in Weirwater.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were the foe in two of the four battle opportunities, in Mareave and Madruga, as the Empire pressed the Broken Shore and fought to reclaim Madruga. They also faced conjunctions in Spiral, Eoradal and Necropolis, where agents sought to escape with intelligence.
n.Highguard: Highguard faced Grendel incursions in Necropolis and scions in Bastion. If the Champion of Loyalty saved the injured thorns on the Reikos border, Highborn military unit captains would be inspired to explore the ruins of Terunael.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs could commit a small force to the season's battles, and the Storm Shaman was charged with defeating the scions at Bitter Hollow in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun pressed their invasion of Kahraman and were met by Imperial armies, while in the north they reclaimed land in Skallahn after the Imperial withdrawal. They and their yegarra were the foe in two battle opportunities, in Liathaven and Kallavesa.
n.Navarr: Navarr could commit one of the largest forces to the battles. In Hercynia the Spear of the Seven and the Archmage of Spring were called to distract vallornspawn so a coven could perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn and repair trods damaged by the scions.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast was the focus of much fighting: Imperial armies met the Jotun invasion of Kahraman and fought to reclaim Madruga, while marked Patricians and a Fire Beacon troubled Segura.
n.The League: The League could commit forces to the battles, and Grendel were reported in Spiral, where the Oblivion Sentinel and the Custodian of the Legacy were called to deal with them.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies may not take the Give Ground order and the Strong Reeds fight harder in Bregasland. Marcher traitors fought alongside Dalton Royse in Liathaven, and creatures needed guiding home in Upwold.
n.Urizen: Urizen could commit forces to the battles and kept its standing advantages for Urizen and Highborn armies fighting between Morrow and Zenith.
n.Varushka: Three conjunctions arose in Karov, against the Festering Warden, the Iron Boyar and the scions. Varushkan armies remained less effective alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies but could take the Hospitality of the Boyars order in Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark could commit the largest force to the battles. Its armies withdrew from Skallahn into Sermersuaq, the Jotun threatened Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and Winterfolk armies kept their honour-bound advantages against the Jotun.

t.Bastion: The Knight-protector of Spring was charged with performing Regrow the Land's Heart and defeating the scions at the Disordered Expanse in Sybella Cross.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the seasonal narrative sweeps over the Bay of Catazar on its way to the Brass Coast.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: listed among military considerations, as the Strong Reeds gain extra strength when fighting there.
t.Brocéliande: Vallornspawn hordes gathered in two places: around a newly found trove of herbs in Black Boughs, and moving through Vale's Lament towards Reikos. Imperial heroes were called to slay both.
t.Feroz: The Champion of Wisdom was called to intercept a suspicious Faraden agent in Taziolar's Woods in Morajasse.
t.Hercynia: A Spring regio, the Toxic Dell in Deer's Folly, offered a chance to perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn if the vallornspawn there could be distracted, and creatures needed guiding home in Summersend.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun invasion continued, but this season Imperial armies stood against it. Conjunctions in Gambit and the Jade Range targeted the Jotun, a Lasambrian champion and an Irremais-marked Patrician.
t.Kallavesa: A battle opportunity arose at Hvalgrunn in West March to defeat Jarl Idunn and his Jotun and yegarra.
t.Karov: Three conjunctions arose: against the Festering Warden in Duzekani, the Iron Boyar in Malimorzi, and the scions in Wieliczka.
t.Liathaven: A battle opportunity arose on the Wyndyn Path in Liath's Ring to thwart Beater Royse, whose Jotun and yegarra were joined by Marcher traitors.
t.Madruga: The Empire fought to reclaim Madruga's shores from the forces that burned Siroc, and a Sunday battle opportunity arose to stop Siakha's cults at Siakha's Maw.
t.Mareave: Five armies fought in Beoraidh as the Empire pursued the conquest of the Broken Shore. A battle opportunity arose to capture the Brine Turtles in Fleisardh, and a conjunction to stop Grendel escaping in Eoradal.
t.Miaren: Aniera Exiles End was named responsible for a meeting with the Burning Vine at the Old Green Fort in Goldglades.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of two territories where any Imperial army may take the Billet order.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: listed among standing military considerations, giving Highborn or Urizen defenders a bonus against attacks from Zenith.
t.Necropolis: Three conjunctions arose: reclaiming an heirloom in Sanctuary Sands, stopping Grendel escaping with intelligence in Longbeach, and defeating Grendel and laying ghosts to rest in Highrod.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan armies can take the Hospitality of the Boyars order there.
t.Reikos: Vallornspawn from Brocéliande threatened to spill into Reikos and slaughter injured thorns at a wayhouse near the Tamarbode border, and the Champion of Loyalty was asked to stop them.
t.Segura: Three conjunctions arose: neutralising the Fire Beacon in Burnish, and destroying Yoorn- and Naeve-marked Patricians in the Sobral Grasses and Lucksprings.
t.Sermersuaq: The Imperial armies withdrawing from Skallahn fell back into Sermersuaq, and a conjunction arose to defeat Freydis and other Jotun in Suaq Fount.
t.Skallahn: The armies attacking the Jotun withdrew, leaving no garrisons, and the Jotun turned to reclaiming land the Empire had taken.
t.Skarsind: The Storm Shaman was called to defeat the scions at Bitter Hollow in Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Spiral: Grendel were reported in Screed and Ossuary, and the Oblivion Sentinel and the Custodian of the Legacy were called to deal with them.
t.Upwold: Any Imperial army may billet in Upwold, and the Keeper of the Golden Fields was called to guide creatures home in Birchland.
t.Weirwater: The Castellan of Spiral Castle was called to defeat the Broken Errant in Weirmoor, and the Knight-protector of Spring to guide creatures home in Wickmoor.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: listed among standing military considerations, giving Highborn or Urizen armies attacking from Morrow a bonus to territory captured.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: The Knight-protector of Spring was charged with performing Regrow the Land's Heart and defeating the scions at the Disordered Expanse.
r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Tancred of the Emerald Dogs found a herb trove guarded by vallornspawn, and the Reeve of Greenforest Fair, Arlen Foreman-Smith, was asked to slay them. Success would yield extra herbs for units questing against the vallorn for two seasons.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: A vallornspawn horde moved towards the Tamarbode border, and the Champion of Loyalty, Dagon, was asked to slay it and save the injured thorns.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Champion of Wisdom was called to intercept a suspicious Faraden agent in Taziolar's Woods.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: The Spear of the Seven, Corwyn Heartsbane, was to distract vallornspawn at the Toxic Dell so that a coven organised by the Archmage of Spring, Ibiss Briarheart, could perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: The Granger of the Golden Orchard was called to guide creatures home from Merel's Glade.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills was called to stop the Jotun on the Path of Sofia.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Mistress of the Dust Parador was called to deal with a Lasambrian champion and destroy an Irremais-marked Patrician in the Parched Range.
r.Karov/Duzekani: The Overseer of the Westward Road was called to defeat the Festering Warden at the Broken Copse.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: The Boyar of the Iron Roads was called to defeat the Iron Boyar on the Granite Path.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: The Champion of Courage was called to defeat the scions at the Glade of Haamrikoht.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: A battle opportunity arose on the Wyndyn Path to thwart Beater Royse's Jotun and yegarra, joined by Marcher traitors.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: A battle opportunity arose to stop Siakha's cults at Siakha's Maw, fought against the Grendel.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Five armies fought here as the Empire pursued the conquest of the Broken Shore.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Vitore Van Temeschwar was named responsible for preventing the Grendel escaping from the Old Skouran Orchard.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: A battle opportunity arose at Brine Blood Bay to capture the Grendel's Brine Turtles.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: Aniera Exiles End was named responsible for a meeting with the Burning Vine at the Old Green Fort.
r.Necropolis/Highrod: The High Exorcist was called to defeat the Grendel and put the ghosts to rest at the Coppice of Athaliah.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: The Imperial Spymaster was called to stop the Grendel escaping with intelligence from Ada's Woods.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Vallornspawn advanced towards the border, threatening injured thorns sheltering at a wayhouse on the Reikos side.
r.Segura/Burnish: The High Bard of the Empire was called to perform Align the Celestial Net at the Ring of Dust and Glass to neutralise the Fire Beacon.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Bakar i Riqueza was named responsible for destroying a Naeve-marked Patrician and recovering dust at the Parched Springs.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind was called to rescue a magician and destroy a Yoorn-marked Patrician in the Parched Grasses.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Custodian of the Pride of Ikka's Tears was called to defeat Freydis and the other Jotun in Hanleth's Wastes.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Storm Shaman was called to defeat the scions at Bitter Hollow.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Custodian of the Legacy was called to stop the Grendel at Lucia's Grove.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Oblivion Sentinel was called to kill the Grendel at Sabina's Sward.
r.Upwold/Birchland: The Keeper of the Golden Fields was called to guide creatures home from James' Orchard.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: The Castellan of Spiral Castle was called to defeat the Broken Errant at Roland's Stand.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The Knight-protector of Spring was called to guide creatures home from Regan's Glade.

Amend Spires of Dusk.d: Proposed by the senator for the Barrens and seconded by Redoubt, the motion amended the Spires of Dusk as described in the Three Keys Wind of Fortune. No commission was needed, because Mortarion Carver, Castellan of Spiral Castle, paid for it himself. The work cost 50 thrones and 10 wains of white granite, which he provided after the Spring Equinox, and took three months. Once it was finished, the Spires of Dusk, also called Houndsgate, had been remade. The last traces of Druj power were gone, replaced by an imposing symbol of Imperial rule. It signals to the Empire and to every sept in the Barrens that the territory is Dawnish, now and in the future.

n.Dawn: The remodelled Houndsgate honours the sacrifice of the Hounds of Glory and proclaims to the Empire and the Barrens septs that the territory is Dawnish, now and for the future.
n.Druj: The last traces of Druj power were removed from the Spires of Dusk and replaced with a symbol of Imperial rule.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the work was paid for by Mortarion Carver, who holds the title Castellan of Spiral Castle.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the work was funded by Mortarion Carver, Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.The Barrens: The territory's fortification, the Spires of Dusk, was rebuilt over three months as Houndsgate, a monument to the Hounds of Glory and a clear statement of Dawnish rule over the Barrens.

An angry blade.d: The motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by The Barrens, followed the attack on Madruga. Graciana, a former corsair, found that only a new Imperial navy would let fleets fight the Grendel's four known navies directly. She proposed a shipyard at Elos, new cranes at Cargo and docks at Nostos; if all three were built, Urizen could support a navy alongside the Citadel Guard. She also proposed the Free Docks, a fortification in Free Landing that fleets could support. Smugglers coves, spy networks for fleets, became a standard commission. Finally, the Red Wind Corsairs could be upgraded to the Forayer quality, letting them switch between army and navy. The Elos and Free Docks opportunities have since expired.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the senators for Miaren and The Barrens proposed and seconded the motion that ordered the appraisal.
n.Grendel: The appraisal was aimed squarely at the Grendel and their four known navies. Graciana judged it debatable whether the Empire could ever fully defeat them without a substantial navy of its own.
n.The Brass Coast: Graciana warned that any navy raised on the Coast would be dangerously exposed after the Grendel burned and then captured the Atalaya shipyards. She proposed fortified Free Docks to protect Madruga and an upgrade letting the Red Wind Corsairs put to sea as a navy.
n.Urizen: Urizen was offered the chance to commission its own navy alongside the Citadel Guard through a shipyard at Elos, cranes at Cargo and docks at Nostos. The Penumbral Watcher's Night mages could shroud the Elos works from Grendel spies.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that many Wintermark heroes prefer ransoming defeated enemies to butchering them, so they have no reason to dislike fighting alongside a daring army like the Red Wind Corsairs.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay was the focus of the appraisal. The proposed Forayer quality would let the Red Wind Corsairs switch between army and navy only in its coastal regions, and fortifying the Bay was judged a very sheer cliff to climb.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Mora's Rock fortification in Feroz is recalled as having been traded to the Grendel years ago, and an earlier fleet spy network there is cited as the model for smugglers coves.
t.Madruga: The recent Grendel attack on Madruga ruined the Salt Guard and drove the appraisal. The proposed Free Docks would make Madruga harder to attack from the sea, but could not sensibly be built while the Grendel held it.
t.Morrow: Graciana proposed new docks at the Conscious River near Canterspire. They would create the Architect of the Conscious River sinecure and raise Canterspire's weirwood output by four wains to 26 each season.
t.Redoubt: Graciana's plans included upgraded cranes at Cargo, costing 25 mithril and 75 crowns, which would raise the level of investment for businesses in Redoubt. They formed one of the three commissions needed for a Urizen navy.

r.Madruga/Free Landing: Graciana proposed the Free Docks, fortified jetties and docks across Free Landing's islands. Imperial fleets could support them as a basic fortification against attacks from the sea, though this opportunity has since expired.

Below the red rock.d: Four Jotun armies (the Escuta, Hierro, Skjalderborn and Corazón) faced two Imperial armies. The fortresses of Cathan Canae's heralds kept the orcs out of the mountains, so they focused on Gambit and Jade Range. They are now four-fifths of the way to conquering Gambit. The Empire won the battle west of Rojota, but lost nearly fifteen hundred soldiers over the season. No building materials were stolen, but the road project made no progress. Corazón raiders took 6 wains of mithril and 7 of white granite. Spring-magic rain fell, and the Red Depths were completed. A raiding warband, accompanied by heralds of Cathan Canae, must be stopped by the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs' general refers to the Marches answering 'the Grendel atrocities'.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun pushed to within a fifth of conquering Gambit and stripped mithril and granite from the hills, despite their defeat at Rojota. New forces joined them, including Yantan Tethrasson's young warband and Fisher-reinforced yeggara, and there were rumours of a new Jarl of Briante.
n.Navarr: Isaella's Dance, under General Ioan Longshadow, advanced cautiously into Kahraman. It helped win the battle for Rojota but shared in losses of nearly fifteen hundred Imperial dead.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn's own territory was invaded again. The Red Wind Corsairs helped save Rojota, but their mines lost mithril and granite, road-building stalled, and the completion of the Red Depths brought a symbolic flowering to Serra Damata.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a handful of League free warriors fought alongside the Red Wind Corsairs.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs' general praises Marcher allies, and traitorous Mournwold humans fight among the Jotun.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman remained a battleground. The Jotun advanced in Gambit and raided mines and builders, while the defences of two Imperial armies and three magical fortresses kept Rojota and the mountains in Imperial hands.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Spring-magic rains were assumed to be an attempt to contain the Blightheart of Madruga.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the yeggara of Mournwold, bolstered by Fishers under Stephen of Sarcombe, fought with the Hierro in Kahraman.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs' general calls on the Freeborn to take the fight to the tribes of Reinos.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: an enchantment helped the Red Wind Corsairs march from Skallahn to Kahraman.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Corazón raiders targeted caravans carrying stone from Serra Damata down into Tassato.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Hierro ground down resistance in Gambit, which is now four-fifths conquered. Imperial forces won the major battle west of Rojota, and the town remains in Imperial hands.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The orc armies focused their raids and probes on Jade Range's plains. Without the Imperial armies and fortresses they would have made significant headway here, and the Blightheart threatens to spill over into the region.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: An enchanted fortress looms over Briante and kept out all but cursory raids. Corazón raiders still stole 6 wains of mithril from the Great Mine, and Chana Aran is rumoured to have been recognised as Jarl of Briante.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Jotun scouts were repulsed from the foothills, and the Damatian Cliffs lost 7 wains of white granite to raiders. Work on the Red Depths was completed and red and gold flowers bloomed across the scarred mountains.

Burying the lede.d: The Asavean Plenum, angered by the Synod's missionaries, discussed sending the Grendel more warships, coin, mithril or weirwood. That aid was stalled until "the Sanguinosa Incident" was resolved. Some Plenum members blamed the Empire for the Tarquinius murders and called for assassins, so Imperial ambassadors were warned. The Duke of Arbonne auctioned salvage rights to Golden Fleet wrecks, offering either weirwood for up to four years or relics. The Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy controlled a 20-person conjunction to the auction. Grenehal Chusciorzi would visit Anvil to meet the kraken-slayers. The Bedelaar Huisbaas offered blight help once the Dry Patricians were defeated. Ehsan's sibling would discuss peace, and the Golden Sugar Cartel made its free ambassadorial message service permanent.

n.Grendel: Asavean warships and marines already backed the Grendel, and the Plenum weighed further aid that was blocked until the Sanguinosa Incident was settled. The Grendel were also invited to the Golden Fleet auction, and Ehsan's sibling was coming to Anvil to discuss Beoraidh, Sinfoyard and peace declarations.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named on the page; its only link is Otkodov's appearance in the list of the Empire's smaller neighbours.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named directly; the page recounts Asavean warships aiding the Grendel, including the destruction of the Isle of Osseini settlement and the burning of Siroc.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller neighbouring nations that exert unexpected influence over the Empire.
t.Sea of Snow: News of the first kraken killed in the Sea of Snow in living memory reached Faraden. A scion of the Caitun Chusciorzi merchant family was coming to Anvil to meet those responsible.

Cities of the Iron Labyrinth.d: Estavus made mystic scrolls of Accoutrements of War, Ramparts of Ashlar and Hammers of Fury available through Before the Throne of Estavus, each requiring a rune of Lann and costly materials. Her Architects of Iron and Stone offered, for a rising price, to assess mithril or white granite bourse seats if the Conclave asked. Her herald Illia sold limited magical items at the Anvil regio, and Hand of the Maker was eased to magnitude six with warm ashes at the Imperial regio. Varushkans remained barred from Before the Throne of Estavus. Ephisis reported gluts of mana crystals and mithril and dearer beggar's lye and tempest jade, and withdrew last season's Grendel deal. The Lictors' agent Oathsmith would meet Ashborn Trosk's representative, while the City of Locks remained in turmoil.

n.Grendel: The deal between the Grendel and the Empire, brokered by the City of Gold and Lead the season before, was declared no longer available.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a League reckoner described the transformed Lictors as "smart", and the opening fiction likened the haggling herald to a Sarvos street urchin.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the City of Gold and Lead's glut of mana crystals was attributed to sales by warlocks of the Frozen North.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction showed Urizeni magicians of a spire selling tempest jade to a herald of Ephisis, and the page noted the scroll rituals could not be added to Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Estavus's year-long injunction still stood, so Varushkan magicians could not use Before the Throne of Estavus to take up any of her offers; their mana would be spent and their goods returned.

t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is not named on the page, and its only possible link is the reference to warlocks of the Frozen North selling mana crystals to Ephisis.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page, which features Urizeni spire magicians only in its opening fiction.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction compared the herald's banal patter to that of a Sarvos street urchin.

Construct Eels Landing.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by Therunin, the motion took up the New port, old wine Wind of Fortune. It developed the docks at Eels Landing, ceded them to House Greywater in recognition of their service during the occupation of Bregasland, and granted a market charter funded by House Bolholt and the Black Vigil. The work cost 6 wains of weirwood, 6 of white granite and 36 crowns, and took three months. Orrick and Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold each supplied 3 wains of weirwood and 3 of white granite. Willem Tarne, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Rhys Nighthaven gave money. Once complete, Eel's Landing began growing into a small town, and taxation drawn from Bregasland fell by two thrones a season.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the motion refers only to the occupation of Bregasland when recognising House Greywater's service.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained a chartered market town at Eel's Landing, with docks granted to House Greywater, backing from House Bolholt and the Black Vigil, and lighter taxation drawn from Bregasland.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland's senator proposed the motion, and its completion established a new market town in the territory and reduced the taxation drawn from Bregasland by two thrones a season.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: New docks and a market charter were built at Eels Landing in the North Fens, and the settlement began expanding into a small town.

Construct Feldspar Distillery.d: The commission, linked to the Standing in the sun Wind of Fortune, cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns and took three months to build. Frith, Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov donated crowns after the Spring Equinox, and Irontide Flax provided 4 thrones and 12 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox. The completed sinecure produces 3 realmsroot and 3 of each herb every season. Imperial Orcs with herb gardens can also choose to produce realmsroot when upgrading them. The title is intended for a member of the Yerende sept. There is no legal requirement, but the sinecure will not function if held by anyone from another sept.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc senators gained the right to appoint the Wise Arborist from Winter 386YE, a post that only functions for a member of the Yerende sept. Orcs with herb gardens can now choose to produce realmsroot when they upgrade them.

t.Skarsind: The Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind gained the Feldspar Distillery, a herb garden sinecure producing realmsroot and herbs each season.

r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Feldspar Distillery was built in Solvihill. Each season it yields 3 realmsroot and 3 of each herb to the Wise Arborist.

Construct Flood Defences in Caricomare.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Spiral, the motion needed no commission and was stated to cost 60 thrones. The recorded cost was 12 wains of white granite and 72 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox, Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos provided 8 thrones, 7 crowns and the 12 wains of white granite, and Aloysius di Sarvos gave 1 crown. The defences were to be decorated with an elegant letter B and a rose in honour of their supporters. Once complete, they ensure Sarvos will not suffer unduly from flooding should the territory be cursed with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.

n.The League: League citizens, chiefly Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos and Aloysius di Sarvos, paid for the project. It leaves the League's city of Sarvos protected against future flooding.

t.Sarvos: Flood defences were completed at Caricomare with Vandersar aid. They shield Sarvos from undue harm if it is cursed with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.

Construct Happiston Mana Exchange.d: Using the authority of the First Imperial Wayleave, Vivane Knotes announced a 16-wain ministry in Happiston that allows the purchase of mana crystals. Its cost was 16 wains of mithril and 48 crowns, with three months to complete. Morgan Townsend von Holberg met the cost in full after the Spring Equinox 386YE, providing 16 wains of mithril and 6 thrones through the prosperity of Happiston Bakes. With the ministry complete, the new title of Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange was to be elected for the first time at the Summer Solstice 386YE by a Tally of the Votes of Marcher farm owners. This first term was a short one, running until the Winter Solstice 386YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new national title, the Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange, chosen annually by a Tally of the Votes of Marcher farm owners. A Marcher, Morgan Townsend von Holberg, funded the whole construction.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold, held by the Marches, gained a ministry at Happiston where mana crystals can be bought.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Happiston Mana Exchange was built in the Chalkdowns and paid for out of the prosperity of Happiston Bakes.

Construct Iron Grove.d: Using the authority of an Imperial Wayleave, Wren Ironclaw announced the commissioning of the Iron Grove, a sinecure that produces eighteen herbs each season. Standard costs applied: 10 weirwood and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox 386YE, Wren Ironclaw provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood to fund it. The Grove was finished, and its title, Keeper of the Iron Grove, is held with tenure. The Wintermark senators can first appoint it, by unanimous decision, at the Summer Solstice 386YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators gained the power to appoint the Keeper of the Iron Grove with tenure, by unanimous decision, from the Summer Solstice 386YE.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa gained a new herb garden sinecure, the Iron Grove, which produces eighteen herbs each season.

r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Skymark became the site of the completed Iron Grove, a herb garden built with weirwood and crowns provided by Wren Ironclaw.

Construct Mana Sinecure in Kallavesa.d: The motion presented the sinecure as support for small halls that had pooled their resources but still could not afford a wayleaf. It carried the standard costs of 10 mithril, 30 crowns and three months to complete. Funding arrived slowly. Amund en Craite, Acwyn, small donors and Hodwyn Aevardson contributed coin between Summer 386YE and Spring 387YE, and Hodwyn Aevardson also supplied the 10 wains of mithril. With the sinecure complete, the title of Remembrancer of Blood and Salt was to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE, by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new mana-producing title, the Remembrancer of Blood and Salt, and its senators must agree unanimously on who holds it, starting at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

t.Kallavesa: The mana sinecure stands in Kallavesa, completed after the last of the mithril and coin arrived following the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Construct Nostos Docks.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Necropolis. It passed, with the docks to cost 18 white granite and 54 crowns and to take three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged provided 5 thrones, 5 crowns and 18 wains of white granite. Triska Markova added 1 throne and Rhys Nighthaven 1 crown. With the docks complete, the Architect of the Conscious River would be chosen by a Tally of the Votes of Urizen mana site owners. The first election was set for the Summer Solstice 386YE, for a short term ending at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen senators from Zenith and Necropolis proposed and seconded the motion. Urizen's mana site owners gained the right to elect the new Architect of the Conscious River.

t.Morrow: The Nostos Docks were built in Urizen-held Morrow, and their completion established the Architect of the Conscious River title.

Construct Printers' Guild Mausoleum.d: The commission was announced by the Chair of the Wolf rather than passed as a vote of the Senate. It requires 20 wains of mithril and 40 crowns and takes three months to complete, with the mithril provided by the Printers' Guild. Once complete, it creates the tenured title of Custodian of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum, which produces thirteen mana crystals each season. The title is to be appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators.

n.The League: League senators gain the unanimous right to appoint the tenured Custodian of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum, a League guild's monument that will yield thirteen mana crystals each season once complete.

t.Tassato: The Printers' Guild Mausoleum is to be raised in Tassato, taking three months to build at a cost of 20 mithril and 40 crowns.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in K.d: The commission was announced as self-funded by Wolfs Hearth and Embers of Iversgaard. It cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months of building time. Contributions came in over the following year, including crowns from Triska Markova, Amris Johan Merikovich, Tom Keeper of Copperhill, Ivana Petara Vodjavic, Rhys Nighthaven, Vladimir Vladirovich Reznikov and Askien Alanovich Vesimerov. Katya Vasillova Reznikov supplied all the weirwood and white granite after the Winter Solstice 386YE. Once the work was finished, citizens of Karsk began giving 12 crowns each summit to the Virtue Fund through donations to the Iron Hearth.

n.Varushka: A Varushkan territory gained a Prosperous Counting House, largely paid for by Varushkan contributors such as Triska Markova and the Reznikovs. Karsk's citizens now channel donations through the Iron Hearth into the Virtue Fund.

t.Karsk: The Prosperous Counting House was built in Karsk, and its citizens now give 12 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit through the Iron Hearth.

Construct Roads of the Sky.d: The motion took up the opportunity presented by the Road out of nowhere Wind of Fortune to establish skyways across Urizen and into Spiral. It cost 225 mithril and 675 crowns and took fifteen months to build. Funding came from many individual donors over successive seasons from Spring 386YE to Summer 387YE, with large contributions of mithril from Otmar van Holberg, Rhode, Bartimaeus and others. Once complete, the Arch of the Sky, a white granite bourse resource, was allocated as a national seat at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The level of investment for businesses and mana sites in Morrow, Zenith, Redoubt and Spiral rose by one.

n.The League: The League's senator for Spiral proposed the motion, and the skyways brought roads and greater investment for businesses and mana sites to League-held Spiral.
n.Urizen: The skyways were built across Urizen, raising the level of investment for businesses and mana sites in Morrow, Zenith and Redoubt.

t.Morrow: Urizen's Morrow was linked by the new skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.
t.Redoubt: Urizen's Redoubt was connected by the skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.
t.Spiral: League-held Spiral, whose senator proposed the motion, received the skyway roads, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.
t.Zenith: Urizen's Zenith was joined to the skyways, and the level of investment for its businesses and mana sites rose by one.

Construct Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery.d: The Boyar of the Iron Roads announced a ministry in Ossium allowing the purchase of mana crystals, at a cost of 12 mithril and 36 crowns with three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox 386YE Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy provided the 12 wains of mithril and 4 thrones 3 crowns 19 rings, with a further ring in small donations. The ministry was completed, and its holder, the Custodian of the Shchaslyvyy Spile, was to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 386YE by Tally of the Votes of the Varushkan mine and forest owners.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new mana ministry whose Custodian is chosen by the nation's mine and forest owners, largely paid for by the Varushkan Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy.

t.Ossium: The Shchaslyvyy Outpost Sappery was built in Ossium, giving its Custodian a place from which to purchase mana crystals.

Construct Smuggler's Cove in Salt Flats.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Weirwater, the motion commissioned a smuggler's cove in the Salt Flats of Sanath. It was framed as a way to strike at the heart of Druj territory, extend Imperial information gathering, hasten the end of the war and free subjugated peoples. The commission cost 10 white granite and 30 crowns on top of standard costs and took three months to complete. Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka provided 3 thrones, 5 crowns and 10 wains of white granite, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov one crown. Once complete, Imperial fleets could support the cove in the same way military units support spy networks.
