Anatolij Paukov Zorkin's unanimous Varushkan judgement proposed a Hall of Fabric Arts in Karov, perhaps at Vorota, with a grander option that could spark a renaissance in weaving and needlework. Mandates pledged Imperial Orc support of 4 white granite and 8 crowns and Varushkan support of 20 white granite and 40 crowns each season, but only once the Senate commissions the buildings. The Navarr mandate against the Empty Hands in Miaren gave supporting military units two random herbs.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the proposed hall site at Vorota sits on a road leading south-east to Weirwater, bringing merchants with fine cloth.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named directly; it figures only within the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites across the Empire.
n.Imperial Orcs: Gralka's judgement passed 185-23 and Emperor Vesna's mandate committed the nation to 4 white granite and 8 crowns a season for a year towards a Library of Worth. This support only begins once the Senate commissions it, and it bars any other such mandate on the nation in the meantime.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly declared the fight against Cold Sun one with the fight against the vallorn, and its mandate gave two random herbs to every military unit supporting an army against the Empty Hands. Navarr armies faced a morale penalty if no Imperial army attacked Cold Sun in Miaren.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a road from the proposed hall site at Vorota leads south-west to Temeschwar, carrying merchants selling wool, linen and silk.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly; it figures only within the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites across the Empire.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly unanimously called for a Hall of Fabric Arts celebrating weaving and needlework, and its mandate readied 20 white granite and 40 crowns a season once the Senate commissions the hall. A greater hall could double as a school and revive these arts as a celebrated part of Varushkan culture.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Tamazi suggested housing the Library inside The Will of Wintermark, perhaps renaming it, though some worried this might offend the Wintermark.

t.Karov: Karov was the proposed site of the Hall of Fabric Arts, with the civil service suggesting the fortified settlement of Vorota. The hall had not yet been commissioned by the Senate.
t.Miaren: The Cold Sun army Empty Hands remained in Miaren. Units supporting armies fighting it gained two random herbs from the Navarr mandate, and Navarr armies faced a penalty if no Imperial army attacked Cold Sun there.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named; it is linked only through the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is not named; it is linked only through the general account of Cold Sun's attacks on cultural sites.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was the proposed home of the Library of Worth, possibly expanded into a Great Library to give the Sunstorm a monument to their Pride. The location within the territory had not been settled and the Senate had not yet commissioned it.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar lies at the end of a road from Vorota that brings cloth merchants to the proposed hall site.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater lies at the end of a road from Vorota that brings cloth merchants to the proposed hall site.

r.Karov/Wieliczka: Mentioned in passing: Wieliczka is not named; the page refers only to Karov generally and the settlement of Vorota as the hall's suggested site.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: Mentioned in passing: Goldglades is not named; the page refers to the Empty Hands in Miaren generally.

The Pride of Gerallt Brackensong.d: At the Winter Solstice 385YE Halwyn Splitroot's writ of consecration passed the Pride assembly 571-24, prompted partly by the Empty Hands of Cold Sun razing First Voice Glade, Gerallt's memorial in Miaren. The civil service identified three sites: First Voice Glade in Miaren, Foxden Steading in Hercynia and Return in Therunin. Each would host a school of music and performing arts with a garden grown from surviving cuttings. Building it would cost 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns over three months, and it would need true liao to consecrate. Once consecrated, it would give every herb garden in that territory three extra herbs each season. The mandate had to be enacted at the Spring Equinox or the process would begin again.

n.Navarr: The proposed school would honour one of their own exemplars and would especially inspire Navarr pilgrims. Depending on the site, it would celebrate Navarr songs and stories, encourage guides and missionaries of the Way, or remind them of the sacrifice needed to defeat the vallorn.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr striding in the in-character story is travelling towards Sermersuaq.

t.Hercynia: Foxden Steading was one of three proposed sites. A school there would teach Navarr understanding of the Way and the Great Dance, and its herb gardens would gain extra herbs each season.
t.Miaren: The razed First Voice Glade could be rebuilt on a larger scale as a consecrated school and garden, offering a defiant answer to Cold Sun's destruction and extra herbs for Miaren's herb gardens.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: it is the destination of the striding in the in-character story.
t.Therunin: The abandoned steading of Return, where Gerallt died thwarting Yaw'nagrah, could be reclaimed as a memorial school, and Therunin's herb gardens would gain extra herbs each season.

r.Hercynia/Summersend: Foxden Steading in Summersend, where Gerallt studied the Way and became a guide, was proposed as a centre where guides and stridings could gather for spiritual counsel.
r.Miaren/Oakways: First Voice Glade in Oakways, the performing-arts school and garden destroyed by the Empty Hands after the Autumn Equinox 385YE, could be rebuilt as the consecrated memorial.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Return in the Upper Tarn Valley, the abandoned site of Gerallt's sacrifice, could be reclaimed as a school preserving Navarr songs and stories about fighting the vallorn and about sacrifice.

The Prosperity of Good Walder.d: At the Winter Solstice 385YE the Prosperity assembly unanimously urged that Good Walder's Orchard be consecrated with true liao. The civil service also offered two alternatives: Corwin's Thump, which stresses punishing the wicked, and the Abbey of Harry's Pot, which stresses rewarding the virtuous. Either alternative would need a pilgrims' lodge built as a folly, costing 20 white granite and 60 crowns over three months. The Orchard already has a suitable structure. Any consecration would raise the Prosperity assembly's influence. Benefactors it named would gain to their personal resources, and those it castigated or condemned would suffer penalties. The mandate had to be enacted at the summit where it was presented.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a tree-filled site in Dawn was among the many claimed resting places of Good Walder, and Marcher tales of him trace back to soon after the Marchers left Dawn.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a Highguard chantry claiming to hold Good Walder's thighbone was among the many sites the civil service considered and set aside.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a well in Miaren was listed among the many places with a claimed tie to Good Walder.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: dry stone walls in Tassato, said to have been built by Good Walder himself, were among the claimed sites not chosen.
n.The Marches: All three proposed sites for Good Walder's inspirational location lie in the Marches, the nation most closely tied to the paragon. Marcher orders such as the Order of the Sack and the Fellows of the Stout Stick would spread the assembly's rewards and sanctions.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Karov was named among the places where a site could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named among the places where a site could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: a site in Astolat was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a site in Hahnmark was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: a site in Karov was cited as one that could claim to be Good Walder's resting place.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: a well in Miaren was among the claimed Good Walder sites.
t.Mitwold: Two of the three proposed sites lie in Mitwold. One is Good Walder's Orchard south of Hay, which is disputed as his resting place but needs no new building. The other is the Abbey of Harry's Pot, which would need a pilgrims' lodge built.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a site in Necropolis, including a chantry claiming Good Walder's thighbone, was among the claimed resting places.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: dry stone walls in Tassato said to have been built by Good Walder were among the claimed sites.
t.Upwold: Corwin's Thump in Upwold was proposed as a site for a consecrated pilgrims' lodge. Its legend has Good Walder cudgelling a miserly steward into a flock of crows, and the site would focus his inspiration on punishing the unvirtuous.

r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: The Abbey of Harry's Pot in the Golden Downs, home of a miraculous soup pot, was proposed as the site of a pilgrims' lodge. Any additional effects there would centre on rewarding the virtuous and sharing fairly.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Corwin's Thump, a low hill in Ashbrook between Ashill and Stockland with a small shrine kept by the Fellows of the Stout Stick, was proposed as the site of a pilgrims' lodge focused on exposing misers and wastrels.

The cry of gulls.d: The Grendel pressed into Calvos Sound backed by three navies, Asavean warships and the plundering Black Eels, but were broken at Calvos. The Empire then drove them through Lightsea and took Quzar after fierce fighting. Sky Mage Faireoir escaped with treasures of the hakima. About 2,500 Marchers and 1,500 Freeborn died. The Empire holds Torres, Calvos Sound and Lightsea; the Grendel hold Siroc Plains. Siakha's heralds attacked both sides, and Shivaarn's emissary declared the Bay hers. A battle opportunity at Siakha's Maw offered chances to stop kraken eggs and rituals, rescue a captive and protect a spy who could betray Rahab. A skirmish in Feroz targeted a Faraden agent.

n.Grendel: Grendel armies were driven from Calvos Sound and Lightsea with severe losses and now hold only Siroc Plains, while Shivaarn's cultists turned on them at Free Landing and the Salt Lords renounced Siakha.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn captains were urged to protect trading vessels crossing the Bay to Highguard.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is described as Jotun-threatened as the Marcher armies passed through it.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South and Burning Falcon helped retake Calvos Sound and Lightsea at a cost of about 1,500 Freeborn dead. The nation's armies remain in decline until another prosperous coastal region is recovered.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the damaged Spider's Dream bridge hampers armies crossing from the League, and Freeborn ships were asked to protect trade bound for the League.
n.The Marches: Three Marcher armies came from Bregasland to help liberate Madruga out of loyalty to the Freeborn, losing around 2,500 soldiers in the campaign.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn captains were urged to protect trading vessels bound for Urizen.

t.Bay of Catazar: A monster-spawning maelstrom now churns where the Shining Pillar stood, and High Priestess Shivaarn has claimed the entire Bay for Siakha, declaring all who live on its shores her prey.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds marched from Bregasland, which the Marchers had recently liberated.
t.Feroz: The Grendel retreated toward the Feroz border, and a skirmish opportunity tasked the Champion of Wisdom with intercepting a suspicious Faraden agent before they reached Grendel lines there.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies swept through Jotun-threatened Kahraman on their way to Madruga.
t.Madruga: The Empire won back Torres, Calvos Sound and Lightsea at a terrible cost. Siroc Plains stays in Grendel hands and Free Landing has fallen to Siakha's cultists.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies marched through Mournwold en route to Madruga.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: armies moving between Sarvos and Madruga must cross the ruined Spider's Dream bridge.
t.Segura: The Burning Falcon marched from Segura to Calvos Sound, and Freeborn militia in Segura tracked a suspicious Faraden agent heading for Feroz.
t.Shayeel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel Storm Lord compared the Freeborn's fury to the winds of Shayeel.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: armies moving between Tassato and Madruga must cross the damaged Spider's Dream bridge.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon dodged orc armies in Jade Range on its way to Calvos Sound.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Grendel assault on Calvos was broken in a bloody battle that left the town standing and free, though Siakha's heralds emerged from the sea that night.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing has fallen to Shivaarn's Siakha cult at Siakha's Maw. An opportunity was offered to stop their kraken eggs and Spring rituals, free Mohrain Luain and protect the Sea-Wraith's informant.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Lightsea was liberated after fighting across its grasslands and a fierce battle for Quzar, which freed the Parador of Salt and Sand. Siakha's cultists later sent Shivaarn's emissary to Quzar's docks.
r.Madruga/Torres: Torres was the Imperial mustering point and remains in Imperial hands. Marracossans from Trajadoz joined the Freeborn armies there to defend their new home.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: A suspicious Faraden-garbed agent entered Yellow Chase and fled from citizens as they headed towards Feroz.

The three pillars.d: The Zenith senator's motion to have Urizeni generals appoint the Warmage failed scrutiny. The Court instead had the Speaker raise two alternatives. Either would make the Warmage an Urizeni national title, appointed by Urizeni magicians in the Hall of Worlds or by the Senate. Each needs a two-thirds constitutional vote and the Throne's ratification. If either passes, Tiborion of the Endless Horizen's followers will stand down and move to Zenith, Morrow or Redoubt. Actius is already satisfied, so the Empire would regain Ankra. Caela of the Silver Flame still holds Cinion, waiting for a Grendel conquest. Two conjunctions target Grendel near the Black Plateau and a raid on the Legacy.

n.Grendel: Grendel mercenaries were found sheltering near the Black Plateau, and Maistir Orla's surviving company was moving to raid the Legacy's mithril. Caela's rebels hope Grendel will invade and conquer Spiral.
n.The League: The League's newly allocated territory of Spiral faced open Urizeni secession, though it was growing prosperous on Lorenzo's mana. Taskel Di Apulian, as Custodian of the Legacy, was charged with stopping a Grendel raid on it.
n.Urizen: Urizen was offered a chance to make the Warmage a national position, elected by Urizeni magicians or appointed by the Senate, to win back Tiborion's rebels. Caela's faction still demanded Spiral's return, and the Shuttered Lantern was sent to investigate.

t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Maistir Orla's mercenaries had been assumed to have fled across the mountains to Mareave.
t.Morrow: Morrow is one of the territories where Tiborion's magicians would resettle and petition to rejoin the Empire if a Warmage motion passes.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt is one of the territories where Tiborion's magicians would resettle and petition to rejoin the Empire if a Warmage motion passes.
t.Spiral: Spiral's spires in Ankra and Cinion remained in open revolt against League rule. Grendel mercenaries lurked near the Black Plateau and threatened the Legacy.
t.Zenith: Zenith's senator raised the failed Warmage motion, and the territory is one of the possible new homes for Tiborion's returning rebels.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra remained in rebel hands, but the Empire would regain control if the Senate passes either Warmage motion, since more than half the rebels would stand down.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion stayed under Caela of the Silver Flame's control whatever happens and was not considered under Imperial control.

They bit the cats.d: Rats attacked tourists at Virtue's Respite and gamblers at Lorenzo's Great Game, and partially devoured the apothecary Ernesto di Temeschwar. Someone wrote "SHADOWSMITH IS DEAD YOU FOOL" in his blood. Theories ranged from a buried Varushkan Sovereign to a Skathe-like curse. The Temeschwari Chamber of Commerce was asked to vote on three options: hiring the Wardog Kennels for 10 Thrones, poisoning the rats with the Guild of the Green Flower, or riding it out. The Synod and Conclave orders were invited to investigate. League military units could take paid but risky rat-hunting work. At Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, a fell wind left workers who had handled sinkhole wealth sick, and the Fox and Fowl Company sought Conclave help.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a party of Imperial Orcs visiting Empress Giselle's tomb was swarmed by rats, and several were bitten.
n.The League: The League's city of Temeschwar faced a rat menace, and its Chamber of Commerce had to choose a response. League military units were offered well-paid but dangerous rat hunts in the sewers.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's old Vard heritage, including the volodny Shadowsmith and a possible Sovereign beneath the city, was suggested as a possible root of the trouble.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk tourists were bitten at Virtue's Respite, and the Steinr grimnir Kylara was eligible to vote in the Temeschwari Chamber of Commerce.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the murdered apothecary Ernesto came from Holberg, and the Hag Queen's earlier curse there, which brought a tide of rats, was offered as a possible parallel.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as the home of Empress Giselle, whose tomb in Temeschwar was the site of a rat attack.
t.Temeschwar: The city was overrun by fearless, aggressive rats that killed an apothecary and closed Lorenzo's Great Game. Its business owners had to choose between wardogs, poison or riding it out, while sickness struck workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: ratters from the Kennels of Holfried were suggested as useful protection against the rats.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Mentioned in passing: the fell wind that preceded the sickness at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets was said to have come from the Vardstein Vale.

Under the firelight.d: At Wyndyn Path in Liath's Ring, the Bronze Harvesters of Shikal were clearing forest. If their Bronze Titan were not destroyed, the region would lose its forested quality and up to four Jotun armies would gain resupply. The Mourn traitor Dalton Royse had fled there, leaving Green March under threat while he lived. Five Feni trapped behind Jotun lines might be rescued in return for aid against Liath's Ring. At Hvalgrunn, Idunn Ironjaw carried the Bear Who Swims' banner while Jotun searched for three storied swords, Skofnung, Angrvurdr and Hofnd, amid Night heralds of Janon and a restless ghost. In Sermersuaq, Freydis led a raid on the mithril mine.

n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs who had fought alongside Janon's heralds could draw an extra hero point at Hvalgrunn. They might also earn a boon from the Shadowed Flame's heralds by recounting their exploits.
n.Jotun: The Jotun worked on several fronts: settling cleared Liathaven forest with Estavus' aid, raiding Hvalgrunn to show off the Bear Who Swims' banner and recover three blades to empower their generals, and sending Freydis against the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn who had fought alongside Janon's heralds could use an extra hero point at Hvalgrunn and might win a boon from the heralds. Separately, Royse was linked to the earlier attacks on Kahraman's roads.
n.The Marches: A Mourn beater, Dalton Royse, was exposed as Stephen of Sarcombe's informant and fled to Liathaven. While he lived, Green March was left vulnerable to Jotun invasion.
n.Wintermark: Jotun raiders entered the sacred Kallavesi marshes of Hvalgrunn to hunt for lost Suaq-forged swords near a restless ghost. A Jotun warband also targeted the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq.

t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Dalton Royse was said to have played a small part in preparing the attacks on Kahraman's roads.
t.Kallavesa: An elite Jotun raiding force crossed Hvalgrunn, several days south of Rest, carrying the Bear Who Swims' standard and searching for three lost swords. Night heralds of Janon filled the area with a zealous aura.
t.Liathaven: Heralds of Estavus were clearing forest at Wyndyn Path so the Jotun could settle and farm it, while Wither the Seed continued to blight the territory's natural cycle.
t.Mournwold: The exposure of Dalton Royse as a spy for Stephen of Sarcombe left Green March under threat until he was captured or killed.
t.Sermersuaq: Feather'd Rain's raven warned the Olgafsdottirshal garrison that Freydis' warband was coming to raid the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Its incumbent, Tuija Dunning, was made responsible for defeating them.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Freydis' warband set out from Tromsa and would return there hailed as heroes if its raid succeeded.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Jotun raiders spread across West Marsh into Hvalgrunn, an ancient battleground where Wintermark heroes and Jotun champions alike lie buried.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Estavus' Bronze Titan and harvesters threatened to strip Liath's Ring of its forested quality. Rescuing the trapped Feni could leave the region under threat from the Empire until Winter 387YE.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: Mentioned in passing: West Ranging was noted as the ashen waste that is the one part of Liathaven not covered by forest.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March gained the Under Threat quality while Dalton Royse lived, because he knew its roads, villages and militia defences.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Mentioned in passing: Mount Majastind was cited as a sacred Jotun site that the orcs assumed was as well protected as Hvalgrunn.

Walk with me.d: Vesna looked back on a year of losses and recoveries: two armies lost and two rebuilt, one in Dawn by the Throne's own hand and one through Varushka's prosperity, with a third on the way in the League. The Throne condemned the assassination of Earl Aramis Du Froste, first senator for The Barrens, as cowardice and called him a martyr. Vesna repeated his final call to shelter refugees from Therunin, a call echoed in the Synod by Gwenllain Heart's End, Keziah of the Suns of Couros, Damascius and Travid Longest Path, Therunin's senator in exile. Navarr, Dawn, Urizen and Highguard had already answered, and Vesna asked every citizen to do the same, promising to retake Therunin together.

n.Dawn: Vesna rebuilt an army in Dawn by the Throne's own hand and mourned the Dawnish Earl Aramis Du Froste, Senator for The Barrens, as a martyr for his nation. Dawn was named as one of the nations that had already opened its doors to Therunin's refugees.
n.Druj: The Druj are the enemy whose grasp the people of Therunin are urged to outlast, and the Throne promised that the Empire will one day walk Therunin's trods again.
n.Highguard: Keziah of the Suns of Couros of Highguard echoed the call to shelter Therunin's refugees in the Synod, and Highguard was named among the nations that had answered it.
n.Navarr: The address focuses on the displaced Navarr of Therunin and states that the Empire has not forgotten Navarr. It notes that Gwenllain Heart's End and the exiled senator Travid Longest Path supported the call in the Synod, and that Navarr has already taken in refugees.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Vesna noted that a third army was on the way in the League.
n.Urizen: Damascius of Urizen echoed the call to shelter Therunin's refugees in the Synod, and Urizen was named among the nations that had answered it.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Vesna credited Varushka's prosperity with rebuilding one of the Empire's lost armies.

t.Therunin: Therunin's people are described as displaced, with their senator in exile and the territory in the Druj's grasp. The Throne called on all citizens to shelter them and vowed that the Empire would walk its trods together once more.
